\subsection{Literal scalar charge and linear semantic precision}
This adapts the completed-child argument of RaD and PR23
\cite{rad,pr23} to the selected complex circuit. Its grouped scalar
operation count is bounded by
\[
 G=\sum_{i=1}^3\frac{N_c}{v_{h_i}}
 \bigl[4(c_{h_i}+v_{h_i})+10v_{h_i}+4h_iv_{h_i}
                         +4h_i^2+8h_i+8\bigr]
   =120574759558400.
\]
Four mixer sweeps use $4(c_h+v_h)$ groups; counting inputs as mixer
groups only enlarges the bound. Two source copies and two four-side
injections use $10v_h$. Four expanded center gather/scatter maps fit
in $4hv_h$, and the remaining terms cover center decoding and scalar
normalizations. Orientation matching does not add a new scalar map.
Each group has at most $W_c$ inputs and outputs, fixed bounded
coefficients, and at most seven extra denominator bits. A charge
$2W_c^2$ per group bounds both magnitude and denominator excess.
Define fixed integers
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E&=64(W_c+m_c+G+1)^3,\qquad B=s_c+E,\qquad C_0=32m_cB^2,\\
 \mathcal E&=2GW_c^2+8s_c+4W_c+4+32m_c<E.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last exact comparison pays scalar evaluation, residual and endpoint
phase wrappers, and fewer than $m_c$ tail kernels. Address permutations
preserve coefficient values; their work is charged by the tape interfaces.
The physical role count has not been substituted for a scalar gate count.

Every completed forward or inverse $u$-axis child has coefficients in
$2^{-u}\mathbb Z[i]$ and absolute row sum at most $2^u$.
Indeed $C=((1+i)I+(1-i)X)/2$ and $C^{-1}=-iZCZ$ have those
bounds, which tensor, unit-phase conjugation and address permutations
preserve. A stream entering with magnitude at most $2^t$ and denominator
exponent at most $p+t$ returns with bounds $t+u$ and $p+t+u$.
This holds on every role, including dirty auxiliaries, by the exact
completed endpoint identity. All streams stay on one fixed fine grid;
this is a bound on their exact values, without return-time rounding,
compression, or re-encoding. Unfinished child values remain local while
other parent operands are parked.

Let $A(e)$ majorize temporary magnitude and denominator excess at any
width at most $e$. A direct leaf satisfies $A(e)\le8e$.
With $f=\lfloor e/m_c\rfloor\ge1$, completed children have total
width at most $s_cf$, and the active child has width at most $r_cf$,
where $r_c=35970$. Thus
\[
 A(e)\le A(r_cf)+s_cf+E.
\]
Since $2B(m_c-r_c)\ge s_c+E$, strong induction gives
\[
 A(e)\le2Br_cf+s_cf+E\le2Bm_cf\le2Be.
\]
The leaf case holds since $B\ge4$. Completed disjoint-axis pieces
have total width at most $d$; prefix kernels, outer phases, and
normalization add the retained $18d$. Consequently
\[
 A_{\rm layer}\le(2B+18)d<C_0d,\qquad C_1=1.
\]
Use $p+\lceil C_0d\rceil$ fractional bits and
$\lceil C_0d\rceil+3$ integer/sign bits per component. For
$p=6b_{\rm in}$, $d=\lfloor b_{\rm in}^{\epsilon}\rfloor$ and
fixed $\epsilon<1$, their total width is eventually $O(p)$.

\subsection{Simultaneous row stock and the stopped tree}
The bit interface accepts complete spectator fields and restores
scratch; the complex interface returns every role exactly. For
$j\in\{b,c\}$ choose the least $t_j$ with
$m_j^{t_j}>2r_j^{t_j}$. Exact integer comparisons give
\[
 (t_b,t_c)=(399,832),\qquad
 (r_b,r_c)=(34500,35970),\qquad W_b,W_c<2^{43}.
\]
Then $D_j(e)=t_j\lceil\log_2 e\rceil$ bounds recursive depth using
a conservative global width bound. Nested bit adapters require
\[
 Q=W_c^{D_c(e)}W_b^{D_b(e)}.
\]
A bit adapter consumes its own factor temporarily inside a complex
node and restores it before the next complex child. Both factors are
reserved simultaneously.

Apply individual $C$ kernels once to a physically preceding prefix of
$q_0=\lceil\log_2Q\rceil$ selected axes, retaining their complete
chunks. If fewer axes exist, execute the whole call elementarily.
Otherwise that prefix gives $R\ge Q$ complete rows; pad once to
$Q\lceil R/Q\rceil<2R$. Descendants inherit full active, control,
spectator and inactive fields. Their all-role return restores appended
zero rows to zero, allowing their eventual removal. The prefix remains
in its preceding position and is not transformed again by descendants.

For eventual $e\le Cp$, $p\ge C$ and $\log_2p\ge25$,
\[
 \log_2Q\le\frac{51}{25}K\log_2p,
 \qquad K=43(399+832)=52933.
\]
The sufficient stock is $p^{108000}$, since
$108000-(51/25)K=417/25>0$. The supplementary suffix condition
\[
 b_{\rm in}^{1-\epsilon}>432000(\log_2b_{\rm in}+8)
\]
holds eventually for every fixed $\epsilon<1$. These stocks and the
literal scalar bound instantiate the complete-row proofs in
\path{whole-complex-concatenation.md} and
\path{whole-complex-prefix-and-wrapper-qualification.md}, located in
the RaD report directory cited below.

Stop complex recursion below $d^\beta$. The potential equal to relative
logical volume times $e^\sigma$ contracts by the strict complex
characteristic. Hence total elementary leaf work has exponent
$\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)$. Since $\tau>\sigma$, paid bit-adapter work
sums geometrically with exponent $\tau$; compact reservations have
exponent $\max(1-c,0)$. All remainders and scans are retained, and
unequal child depths require no extra assumption.

\subsection{Adopted analytic and tape proof map}\label{sec:transfer}
PR23's retained composition proof is
\path{references/semantic-bulk/pr23/semantic-bulk-17-note.tex}.
The underlying RaD files below are in
\path{references/semantic-bulk/rad20/reports/}.
They supply analytic and machine arguments, rather than finite-network
counts. The files beginning with \texttt{review-} are retained for their
written mathematical derivations; their historical titles do not assert
a new external audit of this result.

\paragraph{Coordinate routing.}
\path{compact-arbitrary-source-routing.md} proves active-masked
arbitrary-source XOR routing on complete rectangular streams. Its
four-update identity restores temporary and guard digits before source
reload. The actual modular rotations are bijections; exceptional records
are corrected by $TS^{-1}$ at their current addresses using stable
reinsertion into the marked holes. Every extraction, reinsertion and
rewind is paid using the local density bound. Three untouched reservoirs
partition a matching, and two matchings implement a coordinate
permutation. Short coefficient records receive a separate complete
spectator of width $\Theta(p^{1-\epsilon})$ through original chunk
interchanges. With the selected arbitrary-width bit contract, the cost
is $O(Vp^\tau\operatorname{polylog}p+\operatorname{poly}p)$; the
short-width fallback requires $\epsilon>a_b$.

\paragraph{Rounded phase-cell inverse.}
\path{downstream-phase-cell-inverse.md}, with the elimination and error
arguments in \path{review-reusable-banded-inverse.md} and
\path{review-phase-cell-inverse.md}, constructs one global rounded
matrix $H$. Its diagonal is exactly one, gap at least $1/(8p)$,
and inverse row norm at most $8p$. Within a physical phase cell it
is exactly a diagonal similarity of a width-truncated Toeplitz matrix.
Similarity weights are computable downward approximations with a
four-ulp allowance; their ratio perturbation is explicitly bounded.
Short Gohberg--Semencul convolutions, ordered Schur complements and
rounded banded boundary solves have $O(p)$-bit online coefficients.
Exact rational setup is reused once per axis and costs $n^{o(1)}$.
An unconditional conventional multiplier handles the short convolutions.
With $\alpha^2=\Theta(p^r)$, the band obeys $w^2=O(p^{1-r})$.
The normalized inverse has norm at most $1/8$, and its normalization is
\[
 \gamma=d\bigl(2\alpha^2+\lceil\log_2(32p)\rceil+1\bigr).
\]
Thus $\epsilon+r<1$ remains essential. The retained disk and exact
recovery error interfaces are discharged by these rounded-map bounds,
including their logarithmic normalization.

\paragraph{Bulk locality and fixed tapes.}
\path{downstream-microbox-resampling.md} takes principal restrictions
of that same global rounded $H$. For a width-$w$ matrix, powers below
$J$ cannot carry a core row across an artificial boundary more than
$Jw$ away. The two Neumann tails bound the difference by
$32p\,2^{-J/(16p)}$. Choose $J=512p^2$, target core length
$L=2^{\lceil8\log_2p\rceil}$, and halo $A=4096p^3$.
Then the error is below $2^{-16p}$. Require the eventual complement
condition $s_i>2(L+2A+2w)$ and preserve each original physical period
cut in every lifted window. Restricted normalized maps retain norm
headroom, so tensor errors add in row norm without a volume factor.

\path{bulk-resampling-tape-transfer.md} implements those windows by
sequential tape operations. Near-one source halos fit into $L$ slots
using $L\ge64dA$ and the retained capacity $T/S<2$.
Target halos persist with length $L+2A$ and total volume at most
$T(1+2A/L)^{d-1}<2T$. Only the currently moved short field receives
temporary binary padding. Alternating overlap tapes emit windows
monotonically; ordered factor pages are scanned and reused over
complete spectator fields. Crop an axis only after its own inverse
completes, retaining halos on the remaining axes. Final ordered cores
restore the original prime-box row order. This yields
\[
 O\!\left(Tp\left[p^\tau\operatorname{polylog}p
 +d\operatorname{polylog}p+dp^\delta+w^2p^\delta
 +\frac{dw^2p^\delta}{L}\right]\right)+n^{o(1)}.
\]
Every term is represented in the final inequalities below.

\paragraph{Prime supply and complete assembly.}
The prime argument recorded in the banded-inverse derivation and PR23
uses Baker--Harman--Pintz \cite{bhp}: sufficiently large $x$ has a prime
in $[x-x^{21/40},x]$. Packing $d$ disjoint such intervals into the
required window is ensured by $12d^2<x^{19/40}$. It holds eventually
for $x=2^{\Theta(p^{1-\epsilon})}$ whenever $\epsilon<1$.
Distinct odd primes, capacity, and deterministic $n^{o(1)}$ search are
retained. This proves the replacement of the former separate-exposure
restriction. The theorem's prime threshold remains an explicit eventual
dependency. \path{downstream-semantic-child-guard.md} and
\path{downstream-semantic-bulk-assembly.md} explain how the linear
precision and these analytic interfaces give the seven margins; the
network-specific charge and row stock have been re-established above.

\subsection{Exact selected assembly}
\begin{theorem}[Conditional multiplication bound]
Under the retained multiplication theorem and the attributed analytic,
coordinate-routing, Gaussian-map and fixed-tape interfaces just
specified, the selected constructions give
\[
 T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
 \boxed{\kappa=\frac{2504683}{200000000000}
                   =1.2523415\times10^{-5}}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Use the exact rational parameters
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a_b&=\frac{1252373}{10^{11}},&a_c&=\frac{131}{5000000},&
 \tau&=1-a_b,&\sigma&=1-a_c,\\
 \eta&=10^{-8},&\beta&=\tfrac14,&q&=a_b(1-2\eta),&
 \lambda'&=1-q,\\
 \lambda&=\tfrac12(\tau+\lambda'),&c&=q(1+\eta),&
 \epsilon&=\frac{1-\eta}{1+c+q},&g&=\epsilon q,\\
 r&=\tfrac12(g+1-\epsilon),&\delta&=\eta/8,&C_1&=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The complex leaf saving is $(1-\beta)a_c=19.65\times10^{-6}>a_b$,
so the internal paid-adapter exponent is $\tau$, and both internal
and leaf exponents are strictly below $\lambda'$.
The exact certificate evaluates 47 strictly positive constraints:
primitive and stopping ranges; the orderings of $\tau,\sigma,
\lambda,\lambda'$; compact reservation $c>q$, geometry and
superlogarithmic fields; $\epsilon<1$ for precision, row suffix and
prime packing; $\epsilon+r<1$ and
$\epsilon>(1-r)/2$ for normalization and cell/band separation;
the phase-local, boundary, short-record and artificial-boundary
allowances; the literal scalar and product-row gaps; and each of the
seven absorption margins. The explicit definitions above are used in
those comparisons, without floating-point parameter selection.

The seven savings are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{operation}&\text{saving}\\\hline
\text{original prefix}&1-\epsilon(1+c)\\
\text{coordinate movement}&a_b\\
\text{compact phase layer}&\epsilon q\\
\text{bulk exposure}&a_b\\
\text{Gaussian arithmetic}&\min(1-\epsilon-\delta,r-\delta)\\
\text{scalar work}&1-\epsilon-\delta\\
\text{dimension}&\epsilon
\end{array}
\]
Their exact minimum is $g$, and the prefix margin equals $g+\eta$.
The two Gaussian terms are paid separately in their displayed minimum;
the bulk artificial-boundary term has positive additional slack
$8-\epsilon+r-\delta-g$. In exact rational arithmetic,
\[
 g=\frac{6261864812144051252373}{500012523729812144048747627},
\]
\[
 g-\kappa=
 \frac{94455653180082150647362759}
      {100002504745962428809749525400000000000}
 >9.4453287365\times10^{-13}>0.
\]
All fixed logarithms are absorbed by these strict gaps. The constructive
setup, catalogue domination, prime existence and retained analytic
recovery have their additional eventual thresholds. This proves the
stated conditional bound in the fixed-tape model.
\end{proof}
